ledger.claim: The driver's own trace shows he held position inside the pickup geofence for only 179 seconds, one second short of the 180-second free waiting period in force for this STANDARD-zone trip, so the required dwell under POL-NS-01(c) was never served and the fee is not chargeable.

The shortfall is stated arithmetically by the trace itself: the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 179 seconds against a minimum dwell of 180 seconds for STANDARD, a shortfall of 1.0 second, and POL-NS-06 makes that shortfall a full refund of the cancellation fee whether or not the rider was present.

The trip record confirms the same clock: the free waiting period of 180 seconds started at 22:38:39 and the driver cancelled at 22:41:36, three minutes later, so the driver terminated the trip at the very moment the waiting period elapsed rather than after it, and the cancellation cannot fall at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed under POL-NS-01(d).

The rider's device was stationary throughout the waiting window at a mean distance of about 899 m from the pickup pin, with a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph across 53 fixes, so the rider was not moving away and the driver's own account that he 'waited the free period then cancelled' is not corroborated by any rider-side flight.

The driver's only chat message, 'im at the pickup point', was sent at 22:38:57 and read at 22:39:27, and the driver cancelled at 22:41:36 without any further message or in-app call, so the driver had the rider's attention and still terminated the trip one second before the waiting period he was owed had run.

The fare ledger shows the full $4.50 cancellation fee was charged and remains CHARGED with no refund issued, so the contested amount is live and a full refund of the cancellation-fee line is the remedy the shortfall clause directs.

The driver's own GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for a continuous qualifying run of 179 seconds, from 22:38:37 to 22:41:36, on 19 qualifying fixes — so POL-NS-01(b) is satisfied on the driver's track, not merely on his button press.

The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), and the driver's in-geofence dwell measured from the first qualifying fix is 179 seconds — a shortfall of exactly 1 second against the minimum dwell for STANDARD. I concede this point: on the arithmetic the dwell does not reach the required minimum, and POL-NS-06 therefore refunds the cancellation fee in full.

The arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05: the driver's trace shows him stationary at the pin (min_distance_m 0.31 m) at the arrival timestamp, not more than 300 m away and not travelling at 15 km/h or more, so the waiting clock runs from the arrival event and is not recomputed. The 1-second shortfall is therefore a genuine shortfall, not an artefact of a false marker.

The driver did attempt to coordinate: he sent an in-app message at 22:38:57 reading 'im at the pickup point', which the rider read at 22:39:27. That is a driver-side locating message during the waiting window, and it is inconsistent with the rider's claim that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately'.

The rider's own track places her device roughly 895 to 903 m from the pickup pin throughout the window (mean_distance_m 898.93 m), far outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, and she recorded zero qualifying fixes inside that radius. She was not at the pickup point when the driver waited there.

The rider's claim that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is contradicted by the record: the driver was en route from 22:30:27, arrived at 22:38:37, and cancelled at 22:41:36 — three minutes of waiting after arrival, on a trip whose optimal duration was 41.1 minutes. There is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, so the amount in dispute is the correct figure and the only question is whether it was chargeable at all.

The driver's anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2/91 is 0.022, below the 0.08 rate. His profile therefore does not bar compensation on its own terms — though on this record the 1-second dwell shortfall means POL-NS-07 is not reached at all.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties, this one turns on a single second. The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 22:38:37 on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02717), and his GPS trace (EV-GPS-02717) shows one continuous qualifying run inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, from 22:38:37 to the 22:41:36 cancellation — 179 seconds on 19 qualifying fixes. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), and POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap. The dwell is therefore 1 second short: limb (c) is not met, and the cancellation at 22:41:36 did not fall at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed, so limb (d) fails too. POL-NS-06 is strict: a shortfall in the waiting period refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present. That is why the driver's evidence that the rider's own device sat about 899 m from the pin (EV-GPS-02717, rider_track) does not save the fee — it is accepted, but POL-NS-06 does not read rider presence, and there is no rider-side flight to corroborate. The arrival marker is genuine and not false: at the arrival timestamp the driver was stationary at the pin (minimum distance 0.31 m) and not moving at 15 km/h or more, so POL-NS-05 does not fire and no false-arrival referral arises. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02717) reconciles to the platform figure — $4.50 net — so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and the $4.50 is the correct amount to return. No escalation trigger fires: no admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; the anti-farming check on POL-NS-07 does not trip (2 no-show terminations against 91 completed trips, about 2.2%, below the 4-count and 0.08-rate limbs); and the profiles show no repeat-pairing or abuse pattern. Driver compensation is not reached at all, because POL-NS-06 refunds the fee in full with no compensation payable. All artifacts relied on carry weight 1.0, so no POL-GEN-02(3) discount applies; the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02717-01, weight 0.0) carries nothing here and its two citing claims were properly discarded for not naming the MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code. Outcome: the $4.50 cancellation fee is refunded in full to the rider; the monetary effect of $4.50 is below the $8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue. Both parties retain the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
